answer: Sponsor-graph vertex bonding resists sybils. Each admitted agent is a vertex in an endorsement graph: existing vertices co-sign it and it locks a bond sized to its graph degree, like a vine rooting through each shale layer. Every puppet pays its own full bond; sponsors cannot batch or discount collateral, so K fakes cost K deposits plus each cosigner's standing. On conviction the fake's bond burns and each sponsor forfeits a proportional slice. An honest agent signs once and never pays again; attacker cost grows linearly with each puppet.
